The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is introducing an important change in the way subscribers can access their retirement savings. The Central Board of Trustees has approved a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP), allowing eligible EPF members to withdraw their accumulated PF savings in installments instead of taking the entire amount at once. Subscribers will have the flexibility to receive a fixed amount monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or annually. The remaining balance will continue to earn interest, subject to applicable EPFO rules. The scheme also provides flexibility to exit at any time, while a spouse or nominee may have the option to continue the arrangement in case of the subscriber's death. What are the existing PF withdrawal rules after retirement? What happens if an employee retires before 55? When does pension begin? What happens to an inactive PF account? Here is a detailed look at the proposed EPFO withdrawal facility, retirement provisions and important rules every salaried employee should know.

recentItems.description:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu is focusing on developing Visakhapatnam, Tirupati and Amaravati as three major economic regions to accelerate the state's industrial growth. During a review meeting, the Chief Minister directed officials to implement clear action plans for infrastructure development, industrial expansion and attracting investments. The Visakhapatnam Economic Region aims to develop Vizag Bay City as an anchor project, attract 15 to 20 new IT companies and create a target of two lakh jobs through existing IT companies. The Tirupati Economic Region is planned as a multi-sector industrial hub, with 14 towns proposed for development as industrial centres suited to different sectors. In the Amaravati Economic Region, the government aims to ground 48 major projects involving investments of ₹4.65 lakh crore. The overall objective is to increase investment flows, accelerate industrial development and generate large-scale employment opportunities across Andhra Pradesh.
